title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## ASTRA builds autonomous space structure

### The Breakthrough
ASTRA robot assembled a 1.4 m reflector segment on orbit using on‑board autonomy to pick, position, and lock each piece, proving a viable approach for in‑space manufacturing of larger structures.

### The Caveats
The claim of scalable autonomous construction is unsubstantiated because only a single 1.4 m segment was tested with no baseline or comparative assessment.

## Skydio F10 Lightrunner asymmetric drone

### The Breakthrough
Skydio’s F10 places a wing‑tip camera on an extended asymmetric wing and runs a single model‑predictive control policy that handles hover to 100 mph cruise, while the MegaDock arm autonomously launches, captures, and recharges up to five drones for continuous operation.

### The Caveats
Performance claims rely solely on Skydio’s own figures, with no independent benchmarks or comparative data.

## Excavator control via cloud‑based LLMs

### The Breakthrough
Dreamscale fine‑tuned four frontier models on a Takeuchi TB20e excavator, running inference in the cloud at ~15 Hz over satellite links; the best model (ϕ0.5) achieved >50 % success dumping cardboard, showing cloud‑only control of heavy machinery.

### The Caveats
The demo is limited to a single pick‑and‑dump task on one excavator, with no testing of other tasks, robots, or conditions.

## RL gives skid‑steer loader acrobatic control

### The Breakthrough
A high‑fidelity hydraulic simulator trained RL policies that lifted a 5‑tonne John Deere loader onto two wheels and performed spins, bucket swings, and terrain traversal, demonstrating model‑free RL handling extreme hydraulic dynamics.

### The Caveats
Only video demonstrations are provided; there are no quantitative metrics or baseline comparisons.

## Reasoning model controls real dual‑arm robot

### The Breakthrough
The PEAR engine lets a 27B reasoning model learn robot‑use reinforcement learning in simulation, raising LIBERO success to 74 % and achieving 60 % real‑world task success on a dual‑arm robot without demonstrations, while preserving its general reasoning abilities.

### The Caveats
Evaluation was performed on a single dual‑arm platform, leaving broader robot generalization unproven.

## Axonnic EMG sleeve decodes finger motion

### The Breakthrough
A 64‑channel forearm EMG sleeve synchronized with hand‑tracking data trains a model that outputs 20 joint angles and force estimates, maintaining sub‑1.7° error after a single 215‑second session without recalibration.

### The Caveats
The demo only shows one user in a brief test, with no real‑world manipulation or multi‑user evaluation.

## CS‑MPC safety‑aware sampling controller

### The Breakthrough
CS‑MPC embeds contraction‑certified tracking feedback and a control‑barrier safety layer, cutting required rollouts by 7‑20× for a rover and reducing quadrotor tracking error 2‑4× versus MPPI, with zero safety violations in 200 simulated missions.

### The Caveats
Results are demonstrated only in simulation against a single MPPI baseline, with no hardware validation.

## Hidden start‑delay improves hand‑over robustness

### The Breakthrough
Injecting a hidden start‑delay randomisation into the giver during self‑play training raises receiver success with unseen partners from ~31 % to ~80 % after 300 PPO updates, also reducing high‑force contacts 3‑5×.

### The Caveats
Findings are confined to simulation with scripted partners; no real‑robot or human experiments were performed.

## pySLAM flexible visual‑SLAM framework

### The Breakthrough
pySLAM provides interchangeable Python/C++ modules, integrates state‑of‑the‑art depth predictors (DepthAnythingV3, RAFT‑Stereo) and segmentation networks (DeepLabv3, YOLO, CLIP), and supports TSDF voxel hashing and Gaussian splatting for volumetric mapping, enabling rapid SLAM component prototyping.

### The Caveats
The framework lacks quantitative benchmark results or real‑world hardware validation.

### Priority
ASTRA’s on‑orbit autonomous assembly is the first of its kind, showcasing a new paradigm for space manufacturing that could reshape future habitats and infrastructure.

### One action
Track follow‑up DARPA NOM4D releases and watch for any multi‑segment assembly demonstrations.

### What to watch
Heavy‑machinery control is advancing from cloud‑inferred LLMs on excavators to RL‑driven skid‑steer loaders, indicating a trend toward remote‑intelligent operation of large equipment without onboard compute.
